promotion: NOT PROMOTED. Pre-WF ROC@30k is -4.95, far below the bar of 15. The lab's own line says the same ('NOT PROMOTED: pre-WF ROC@30k -4.95 < 15'). The one-episode flag is false but does not matter. The flag is false only because the curve has a single drawdown episode (dd5_n=1, so DD5 = max DD and the 1.3x test cannot trip). The curve peaks near its start and ends at its low, so ROC = -30/years = -4.947 at every cost level. Gross per trade is the number that separates the readings: -0.18 pt (plugin) and -0.21 pt (literal). The best single-slip variant makes +0.015 pt against a 0.783 pt cost. No reading of the text comes near the bar.
degenerate: The premise is wrong: the lab did NOT report 1 trade. numbers_pre_wf.json says trades 1550, trades_per_year 255.6 and trades_total_incl_warmup 1550. pre_wf_trades.csv has 1550 rows and sandbox_pre_wf_out.json lists 1550 trades, and both match the engine trade for trade. The contract smoke gave 386 trades on 2015-01..2016-06 (258.7/yr). The only '1' in the lab numbers is dd5_n = 1, the number of drawdown episodes DD5 averages over; it is not a trade count. That count is 1 because the curve never regains its early high. The plugin is degenerate the other way: it fires every session. My own build of the rule finds qualifying signal bars as follows. Literal reading: 24,803 bars (about 4,090 a year, 8.4% of bars, median 16 per session), in 1550/1550 sessions. The first signal comes by session bar 3 in 1332/1550 sessions, median bar 1. Plugin's reading: 106,678 bars (38% of eligible bars, median 69 per session), in 1550/1550 sessions. In 847/1550 sessions the first signal is the very first eligible bar (session bar 13, entry 09:56). So the break filter barely filters, and the cap of one trade per session sets the count. That is why every knob corner gives the same 386 trades. It is not a units, threshold, session-filter or off-by-one bug. The off-by-one exit (S1) changes holds, not counts. The prereg's prior of 120/yr was simply wrong. Look-ahead is clean: in all 1550 sessions, perturbing every bar from the entry bar on (entry open kept) changed 0 entries, and perturbing every bar after the exit changed 0 exits. The signal reads h/l/c of bar k only and fills at o[k+1]. The stop width w(k) is known before entry. The stop is checked intrabar from the entry bar. The only future reads are the session-length guards; they changed 0 trades (S6), and no session is 15 bars or shorter.

slips_judged.what: S1: time stop exits one bar late (close of bar entry+6, so 7 bars or 14 min from the entry fill)
slips_judged.why: Real, but small. The text pins the hold: '6 bars = 12 min'. The plugin fills at the open of bar e and exits at the close of bar e+6, so the trade is open for 14 min (1023 of 1550 trades run the full hold). The opposing case: the house's own REPLAY_1_0.py uses the same ek_fill + max_hold_bars convention, and the bar stamps are 12 min apart. That convention still does not make the time in the trade 12 min. It does not change the verdict: with the 12-min exit, ROC@30k is -4.95 and DD5 is $28,589.

slips_judged.what: S2: band lookback N is not given; the plugin uses band_bars=12
slips_judged.why: The text gives no N, so any N is a free choice and none can contradict it. 12 sits inside the plugin's own declared 6-30 range. This is a reading choice, not a slip. The verifier's N=20 alternative is also only a pick.

slips_judged.what: S3: the band window includes the signal bar (k-N+1..k)
slips_judged.why: 'Median of last N bars' high-low range', worked out when bar k closes, can reasonably include bar k. The text never says 'prior N bars'. This is a reasonable alternative reading and uses no future data.

slips_judged.what: S4: the band resets each session, so the first signal is at session bar 12 (entry 09:56)
slips_judged.why: The text says 'trailing' and says nothing about session handling. A per-session band is a reasonable reading for an RTH intraday rule, and it keeps the overnight gap out of the band. The text does not forbid it.

slips_judged.what: S5: band centre is the median close of the window, edges are +/- 0.5 x median range
slips_judged.why: The text names no centre. The plugin's band is exactly one median range wide, which fits 'noise band (median of ... range)' and the stop of '1.5x the band width'. The verifier's literal reading (previous close +/- 1w) gives a band 2w wide while keeping the stop at 1.5w, so it fits the text no better.

slips_judged.what: S6: extra guards (skip sessions of 15 bars or fewer; no signal on the last 2 bars)
slips_judged.why: The text says nothing about them. They only use the known session schedule, and they change 0 trades: no session is 15 bars or fewer (shortest 47), and the latest first entry is session bar 53. I confirmed this myself.

slips_judged.what: ALL readings at once (plugin -> literal arm B path)
slips_judged.why: This combines the readings above and is not a separate slip. The cumulative path landing on arm B at 1550/1550 checks the verifier's own coding. Every point on the path has ROC between -4.62 and -4.95, so nothing changes the verdict.

slips_judged.what: Items the verifier says match the text (day trend = close vs session open, entry at next open, 1.5x stop with gap-through filled at the open, flat by the last bar, one trade per session)
slips_judged.why: I confirm all of these. Every entry price equals open[e]. No entry falls on a session's first bar. Every exit price sits inside its exit bar's high-low range. The first signal is the only trade each session. A trade that would run past the session ends at the session's last bar close.
